rules.statement: Register each implementation of an open strategy collection (rules, handlers, validators) as its own class with `TryAddEnumerable`, so a package adds a strategy with one registration.
rules.why: `TryAddEnumerable` keeps one registration per implementation type, so the collection stays open and duplicate registrations cannot happen.
rules.check: Look for multi-implementation services registered with `AddSingleton`/`AddScoped`/`TryAdd*` instead of `TryAddEnumerable`, or several strategies bundled into one class.

rules.statement: Put a cross-field validation relation in one registered rule that a shared validator runs, not in a separate copy inside each caller that stores the entity.
rules.why: Per-caller checks drifted: each caller checked a different subset of the relations, and invalid configurations were accepted.
rules.check: Look for a new or changed write path (API, registration, seeder) that checks relations between settings inline instead of calling the shared validator, or a new relation added to just one caller.

rules.statement: Base a change-detection gate that decides whether to re-run validation rules on the inputs each rule declares, not on a separate hand-written gate per rule.
rules.why: A hand-written gate can leave out an input the rule reads, so a change to that input would skip validation. When one gate uses the declared names, the gate and the rule cannot disagree.
rules.check: Look for a rule that reads a setting or input missing from its declared input list, or for a per-rule 'should run' method that duplicates the inputs the rule reads.

rules.statement: Give a validation violation in an open vocabulary its own human-readable description that names the values involved, instead of a closed enum of violation kinds, and have callers report that description.
rules.why: A closed enum would force every package that adds a relation to edit the enum, but the vocabulary of relations is open.
rules.check: Look for a new enum of violation or error kinds that extension packages would have to extend, or callers that build their own messages from a kind instead of using the violation's description.

rules.statement: Validate each value against its own domain before running rules that relate several values, so the relational rules only see values that already passed the domain checks.
rules.why: Rules then read only values whose domain is accepted, and the cheaper checks run first.
rules.check: Look for relational or coherence validation that runs before, or without, the per-value domain validation of the same document.

rules.statement: In dynamic client registration, return `invalid_redirect_uri` only for a violation of `redirect_uris`, and return `invalid_client_metadata` for every other metadata violation, including `post_logout_redirect_uris`.
rules.check: Look for `invalid_redirect_uri` returned for problems with fields other than `redirect_uris`, such as `post_logout_redirect_uris`.

rules.statement: When a settings write is checked against existing dependent entities, refuse the write only for violations that the change introduces, not for entities that were already invalid.
rules.why: An entity that was already incoherent must not block an unrelated change.
rules.check: Look for write validation that refuses a change because of violations that also exist under the previous settings, with no comparison of before and after.

rules.statement: Run bulk validation scans over stored entities as paged, untracked projections that leave out secrets, under an explicit tenant scope when the endpoint itself is not tenant-scoped.
rules.why: The walk only reads the entities. Leaving out secrets limits exposure, and the explicit scope is needed because control-plane endpoints are not scoped to the tenant they address.
rules.check: Look for scans over all entities that load tracked full entities (including secret columns), skip paging, or rely on an ambient tenant scope from a control-plane endpoint.

rules.statement: Make configuration seeders run the same validation as other write paths before creating an entity, and stop host startup with an exception that names the entity and lists the messages when validation fails.
rules.why: Then the host does not start with seeded configuration that the server cannot honor.
rules.check: Look for seeders that create entities without running the shared validators, or that log and continue on a validation failure.

rules.statement: Cap a validation problem response at a fixed number of errors per key, and add a summary error that counts the rest while every item is still evaluated.
rules.why: A walk over many entities can produce one error per entity. The cap keeps responses bounded and the count stays exact.
rules.check: Look for validation responses that add one error per entity without a limit, or that stop evaluating early so the count is wrong.
